allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each integer n at least 2, among all length n minus 1 sequences of plus or minus 1, determine exactly which sign patterns maximize the number of permutations of 1 through n whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs.
allowed_dependency_manifest.label: root_semantic_sketch

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

payload.role_in_assembly: This is a support lemma for the proof of the bottleneck lemma L6; it controls the monotonicity type of the dynamic-programming state after each step.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2.
The sequence s has exactly n minus 1 entries.
Each entry of s is either plus 1 or minus 1.
The tuple a is a permutation of {1, 2, ..., n}, so all entries are distinct and each integer from 1 to n appears exactly once.
The inequality si times (a(i+1) - ai) greater than 0 means ai+1 is greater than ai when si is plus 1, and ai+1 is less than ai when si is minus 1.
The constraint must hold for every index i from 1 to n minus 1.
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n at least 2, among all length n minus 1 sequences of plus or minus 1, determine exactly which sign patterns maximize the number of permutations of 1 through n whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs.
quantifier_order: First fix an integer n with n at least 2.
Then range over all sign sequences s of length n minus 1.
For a given s, count all permutations a of {1, 2, ..., n} satisfying the adjacent sign constraints for every i from 1 to n minus 1.
Finally, for each n, identify which sequences s maximize this count.

witness_dependencies: The maximizing sign sequence depends on n.
No existential witness is built into the counting definition of f(s); the only counted witnesses are permutations a satisfying the inequalities.
Any characterization of maximizers must be valid uniformly for all sign sequences of the specified length for the fixed n.

domain_restrictions: Each entry x_i is a nonnegative real number
Indices i run from 1 through m
Indices j run from 1 through m plus one
U(x) and D(x) are vectors of length m plus one
Nondecreasing means consecutive entries satisfy U_j <= U_j plus one
Nonincreasing means consecutive entries satisfy D_j >= D_j plus one
Nonconstant means not all entries of the vector are equal
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integer m and every length m vector x of nonnegative real numbers, the prefix-sum vector U and the suffix-sum vector D satisfy U_1 = 0, U at index m plus one equals the total sum of the entries of x, U is nondecreasing, D_1 equals the total sum of the entries of x, D at index m plus one is 0, and D is nonincreasing. If some coordinate of x is positive, then neither U nor D is constant.
quantifier_order: For every length m vector x with nonnegative real entries
Define U(x) and D(x) using the stated formulas for each index j from 1 through m plus one
For every index j in the allowed range, the endpoint and monotonicity claims hold
If there exists an index i from 1 through m with x_i positive, then both U(x) and D(x) are nonconstant

payload.statement_nl: Let m be a positive integer, let x=(x_1,...,x_m) be a vector of nonnegative real numbers, and define vectors U(x) and D(x) of length m+1 by U(x)_j = sum_{i=1}^{j-1} x_i and D(x)_j = sum_{i=j}^{m} x_i for 1 <= j <= m+1, with empty sums interpreted as 0. Then U(x)_1=0, U(x)_{m+1}=x_1+...+x_m, and U(x) is nondecreasing. Also D(x)_1=x_1+...+x_m, D(x)_{m+1}=0, and D(x) is nonincreasing. If at least one entry of x is positive, then both U(x) and D(x) are nonconstant.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let S:=x_1+\cdots+x_m.

By definition,
U(x)_j=\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}x_i \qquad (1\le j\le m+1),
with the convention that an empty sum is 0. Hence
U(x)_1=\sum_{i=1}^{0}x_i=0,
and
U(x)_{m+1}=\sum_{i=1}^{m}x_i=S.

Now fix j with 1\le j\le m. Then
U(x)_{j+1}=\sum_{i=1}^{j}x_i=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}x_i\right)+x_j=U(x)_j+x_j.
Since each x_j is nonnegative, we have U(x)_{j+1}\ge U(x)_j. Therefore U(x) is nondecreasing.

Similarly,
D(x)_j=\sum_{i=j}^{m}x_i \qquad (1\le j\le m+1),
again with empty sums interpreted as 0. So
D(x)_1=\sum_{i=1}^{m}x_i=S,
and
D(x)_{m+1}=\sum_{i=m+1}^{m}x_i=0.

For 1\le j\le m,
D(x)_j=\sum_{i=j}^{m}x_i=x_j+\sum_{i=j+1}^{m}x_i=x_j+D(x)_{j+1}.
Because x_j\ge 0, this gives D(x)_j\ge D(x)_{j+1}. Therefore D(x) is nonincreasing.

Finally, assume that at least one entry of x is positive; say x_k>0 for some k. Since every x_i\ge 0, it follows that
S=\sum_{i=1}^{m}x_i>0.
But then
U(x)_1=0 \quad\text{and}\quad U(x)_{m+1}=S>0,
so U(x)_1\ne U(x)_{m+1}. Hence U(x) is not constant.
Likewise,
D(x)_1=S>0 \quad\text{and}\quad D(x)_{m+1}=0,
so D(x)_1\ne D(x)_{m+1}. Hence D(x) is not constant.

Thus all the stated endpoint, monotonicity, and nonconstancy claims hold.
result_payload.proof_summary: The endpoint values follow directly from the definitions and the empty-sum convention. For each j=1,...,m, one has U_{j+1}=U_j+x_j and D_j=D_{j+1}+x_j; since x_j>=0, U is nondecreasing and D is nonincreasing. If some x_k>0, then the total sum S is positive, so U_1=0 differs from U_{m+1}=S and D_1=S differs from D_{m+1}=0; hence both vectors are nonconstant.
